contrasts.line: Tiptoeing is quiet and careful. This walk is loud, proud and in step.
Trudging drags with tiredness. This walk is brisk and full of energy.
A stroll wanders with no hurry. This walk keeps time, like a drumbeat.
Limping is uneven because something hurts. This walk is strong and even.
Marching is loud and firm. The cue asks for silence.
Trudging is heavy and tired. This walker is light and careful, staying quiet.
Strolling is relaxed, not secret. This walker is trying not to be noticed.
Limping means a sore leg. This walker steps lightly on purpose, to stay silent.
Marching is quick and sharp. This walker is worn out and slow.
Tiptoeing is light and silent. These steps are heavy with tiredness.
A stroll is easy and fun. This walk is hard work, every single step.
Limping means pain in one leg. This walker is exhausted all over, not hurt.
Marching keeps strict time. This walk is easy-going, with no hurry at all.
Tiptoeing hides you. This walker is out in the open, enjoying themselves.
Trudging is slow, tired work. This walk is light and happy.
Limping is sore and uneven. This walk is comfortable and easy.
Marching is strong, even steps. These steps are uneven because something hurts.
Tiptoeing is quiet by choice. These steps are uneven from pain.
Trudging is tiredness all over. Limping favours one hurt leg.
Strolling is easy and comfortable. This walker hurts with every step.

meta.scrub_note: Pilot seed set, hand-authored. Revision 2 after the first judge-uniqueness run: killed 4 sentences whose cues admitted a second manner or clashed with the pinned sense (regularity-of-schedule read as stroll; determined-walk and walk-to-a-destination reads vs march.v.03/stroll.v.01), and sharpened 9 trudge/limp cues so exhaustion-vs-injury is carried by the sentence (group+slow for trudge; one-sided injury for limp).
